item.title: Iraola, Gakpo and Barcola Reflect on Arsenal Defeat Before Fenerbache
item.description: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola during a press conference at Saracoglu Stadium, Istanbul. Picture date: Tuesday November 3, 2026. (Photo by Adam Davy/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images After a big, controversial match against Arsenal over the weekend, it feels like there’s been a bit of a hangover. But the fixtures keep coming, and Liverpool FC are in Champions League action next, playing Fenerbache in Istanbul. At the pre-game press conference, Iraola had this to say about the difference between Liverpool in Europe and domestic action this season: “In the Champions League we’ve been scoring a lot of goals, being very good offensively. In the league that’s probably the worst part. We are defending very well but it’s costing us to score.” “But it’s still early in the season. We’ve had good games. It’s a process and we will definitely improve.” Cody Gakpo chimed in, speaking on Liverpool’s failure to register a shot on target in the Arsenal game: “Not really. For that game, yes, because you need to shoot on target to score, but if I look back at the games we’ve played, we have created some chances, scored goals, so it doesn’t really worry us.” “We would love to score more goals than we have up to now, but looking at the quality we have up front and in midfield, I don’t see that as an issue.” Bradley Barcola on the Arsenal defeat. 🔴 pic.twitter.com/gLpIr0oMGr https://t.co/4oNvH05dDz — AS (@Anfield_Sector) November 3, 2026 In a separate interview with LFCTV, Bradley Barcola, seated together with Jérémy Jacquet, was asked if the defeat to Arsenal changes the team’s goals for the season: “I don’t think it has changed the goals for this season. We had the chances to score, even to win the match.” “Often, when we’re in a game like this, we resort to long balls, but in my opinion, we should try to keep the ball on the ground more, because we have the players with the quality to do that.” “We are not going to give up. We know that other teams will drop points. So it’s down to us to remain consistent until the end of the season.” Obviously, 0 points from 6 at home against Manchester City and Arsenal is a big blow, but there are positive signs in how the team has managed to churn out results despite prominent issues in the squad. The Reds will have a big chance to bounce back against Fenerbahce and go on another run.

item.title: 'We learned some great lessons': McCullum reflects on Pakistan setback ahead of Australia challenge
item.description: England head coach Brendon McCullum is hoping his team can turn the disappointment of their recent ODI tri-series campaign in Pakistan into valuable lessons as they prepare for a challenging white-ball tour of Australia. England arrived in Perth on Monday for an eight-match assignment against Australia, featuring three ODIs and five T20Is. The series gets underway on November 13 and will serve as an important part of their preparations for next year's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, according to the ICC website. The tour also marks England's return to Australia following their disappointing Ashes campaign earlier this year. However, McCullum is keen to look forward rather than dwell on the past, viewing the upcoming contests as an opportunity to assess his team's progress and methods. "Firstly, it's nice to be back. An Australia tour is always a great tour. The cricket's always pretty competitive. We'll play at some great stadiums, against a good side, and continue to test our methods, towards the one-day World Cup," McCullum said. The England coach also stressed the importance of maintaining an aggressive approach while using the demanding schedule to improve the players' fitness. "We know we need to keep getting better, but we've been presented with some good opportunities, and this will be one of those in the next couple of weeks. We want to play a high-octane, robust style of play, which demands fitness elements to it. So for us, this is a great opportunity to have a little fitness block in and around the demand of this series," he added. McCullum keen to build on Pakistan tri-series experience England had a mixed outing in the ODI tri-series in Pakistan, where they managed only one win across four matches and failed to secure a place in the final. There were, however, encouraging individual performances. Captain Harry Brook and opener Ben Duckett impressed with the bat, while Liam Dawson, Sonny Baker and Jamie Overton contributed with the ball. Despite falling short of their target, McCullum believes the tournament offered important exposure, particularly for a relatively inexperienced squad that needs more time in one-day cricket. Reflecting on the campaign, he admitted that the result was disappointing but highlighted the benefits of facing different opponents, adapting to varying conditions and dealing with different tactical challenges. "It was disappointing. Obviously, it was great to play in the tri-series. With the view towards the World Cup, the ability to be able to bounce between games, and different tactics, and different oppositions was good," McCullum said. item.title: Holland boys cross country qualifies for state for first time in 30 years as area's historical run continues
item.description: Cross country continues to make history in the area. In the past five years, the West Ottawa girls, Holland Christian girls and Holland Calvary boys have won state championships. The Maroons and Owls look poised to repeat this season. The area has seen 20 regional title teams in the past three years and 10 individual regional champions during that time. Last year, the Holland girls made the state finals for the first time in 30 years. They made it again this year, but it was the Holland boys' turn to make some history, making their first state finals as a team in 30 years. More: Five cross country teams claim regional titles; 9 teams, 8 individuals qualify for state Ten of our 19 high school teams made state last year and this year, it is nine - and that was close to being 12 as three teams missed by a single spot, including the Fennville boys who were looking to qualify for the first time in nearly 50 years. Success has become commonplace around the entire area. It started with Saugatuck, which has enjoyed two decades of contending teams, both the boys and girls. The other schools have followed with four individual state champions on the girls side and nearly 100 all-state performances - and that is coming from every school. This year, it was the Holland boys turn to snap a long skid and get back to state. The Dutch are lead by two multi-sport athletes. Aiden Lambers has qualified for state as an individual, but is also a state qualifier in swimming. Meanwhile, Caelen Gray plays on the soccer team, which could make for a crazy Saturday if he runs in the cross finals at Michigan International Speedway and Holland is in the soccer finals. The Dutch have to win in Wednesday's semifinal for that to happen. Holland has a lot of young runners on this team, so the Dutch are looking to make this a regular thing, as the girls have. State championships will likely be won by area teams and nearly all of our schools will have at least one all-state runner. It is incredible that this level of talent has been sustained in one area for so long. And based on this year's group, the underclassmen and the middle school success - it isn't going anywhere. item.title: Liverpool star admits he’s not shown his best this season
item.description: Liverpool star admits he’s not shown his best this season Bradley Barcola on Liverpool Move, PSG Exit and Handling Salah Comparisons Bradley Barcola has offered a clear insight into the early months of his Liverpool career, addressing his big-money transfer from Paris Saint-Germain, the challenge of settling at Anfield and the inevitable comparisons that followed Mohamed Salah’s departure. The France international arrived in a deal worth £123m and, with that fee attached, scrutiny was always going to follow. Liverpool had already committed vast sums to reshape their attack, with Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz among the headline arrivals of the past two years. Barcola’s move placed him firmly in that same bracket, a premium signing expected to make a premium impact. His start was not especially explosive. Across his opening 10 matches for club and country this season, there was no goal and no assist. For a player signed to operate in one of the most closely examined attacking roles in English football, that immediately drew attention. Yet recent performances have offered a more encouraging picture. A hat-trick against LASK in the Champions League was followed by assists in wins over Brighton and Brentford, and while he did not produce a decisive contribution against Arsenal, his running and movement caused problems in the first half. Even so, Barcola does not believe Liverpool have yet seen the best version of him. He feels there is more to come once his understanding with team-mates develops further and patterns of play become more instinctive. Internally, there is a sense that improvement is ongoing, with colleagues adapting to his style and Barcola growing more comfortable with the demands of the Premier League. Photo: IMAGO PSG Exit Shaped Barcola’s Liverpool Decision Barcola’s decision to leave PSG was not made lightly. He departed having collected major honours and having been part of a dressing room he viewed as close-knit, but the timing felt right for a new step. He had enjoyed success in Paris and leaves with his reputation enhanced, yet there was also a feeling that his role had limits. At PSG, he was trusted regularly in domestic competition and contributed to title-winning campaigns, but in the biggest European ties he was often behind others in the attacking pecking order. With fierce competition around him, that was understandable, though it also helped shape his outlook. He wanted a fresh challenge, more prominence and a different environment in which to build his own story. Liverpool’s interest resolved any uncertainty. Once the opportunity presented itself, Barcola was convinced by the scale of the club and the project on offer. From his perspective, there was little hesitation. item.title: Sunderland are in the race to sign midfielder with £33m release clause
item.description: Sunderland are in the race to sign midfielder with £33m release clause Sunderland Tracking Stefan Dzodic as Atletico Madrid Lead Midfield Race Sunderland are among the clubs monitoring Stefan Dzodic, with Atletico Madrid currently leading the chase for the highly rated Almeria midfielder, according to TeamTalk. The 21-year-old has emerged as one of the more intriguing young operators in the market, and there is a growing sense that his situation could gather pace over the months ahead. Dzodic, a Serbian international born in France, is under contract at Almeria until 2032 and has a €40million, £33m, release clause. That figure, allied to Almeria’s secure negotiating position, means any suitor will need to move seriously if interest turns into action. As reported, Atletico have already “opened discussions with the player’s representatives”, a notable development even if the move is being shaped with 2027 in mind. The Spanish side see him as a long-term investment and are working early. That alone tells its own story. When a club of Atletico’s level starts laying foundations well in advance, it usually reflects conviction in both the talent and the trajectory. The report adds that “Atletico are as it stands are best placed to sign Dzodic”, which places the Premier League clubs watching him in a reactive position for now. IMAGO Stefan Dzodic on Sunderland shortlist Sunderland’s interest is described as genuine, even if not yet advanced. Bournemouth, Brentford and Brighton are also in the frame, with all four English clubs having tracked his development since his 2025 free transfer from Montpellier and his “growth into a regular in Almeria’s midfield”. For Sunderland, that kind of profile makes sense, young, upwardly mobile, physically strong and tactically flexible. Dzodic is said to have “impressed with his physical presence, composure on the ball and ability to play in both defensive and more attacking midfield roles”. At 6ft3in, he offers stature, but the more relevant detail is that he appears comfortable across different midfield functions. That broad skill set is often what drives competition in this section of the market. Atletico Madrid pressure could shape next move There is no indication yet that Sunderland are close to making a formal move, and Almeria are under no pressure to sell in January unless the clause is triggered. Still, the picture is clear enough. Atletico’s activity has elevated the situation and may force others to decide whether they are merely monitoring or preparing to act. This season, Dzodic has made 10 appearances in all competitions, recording one goal and one assist. He has also made his senior Serbia debut, another factor that has “further raised his profile”. Sunderland will know they are not alone here, but they remain in a race that looks open, competitive and worth watching closely. item.title: Premier League civil war erupts as rival clubs demand SECOND investigation into Manchester City finances
item.description: Khaldoon City fans - Getty A major rift has emerged between Premier League clubs as a selection of rivals push for a fresh investigation into Manchester City’s financial affairs. Despite the Etihad giants already facing the fallout of 114 guilty verdict, there is a growing appetite to scrutinise the club’s books for the period following 2018. Fresh scrutiny for the Manchester giants Following September's confirmation that Manchester City were found guilty of 114 financial charges , several top-flight rivals are now demanding further action, according to reports. The initial verdict covered alleged rule breaches between 2009 and 2018, but there is mounting pressure to examine the club's financial conduct in the years since. However, this push has created a distinct split among Premier League chief executives. While some factions want immediate scrutiny of the post-2018 period, others are hesitant to trigger another drawn-out legal battle that could further damage the division's reputation. Questions over sponsorship deals A major point of contention stems from the independent commission's findings regarding City's sponsorship agreements. The initial ruling highlighted deals that were allegedly disguised as owner investment. According to The Independent , rival executives remain sceptical that these practices abruptly stopped, questioning if anything actually changed after 2018. The commission also established that the club and their Abu Dhabi-based sponsors were related parties. Rival officials believe that if this relationship remained unaltered, it provides a solid foundation for additional charges in subsequent seasons. Conversely, the ongoing saga has already caused widespread disillusionment across English football . Some chief executives fear that pursuing a second case could create severe awkwardness for the sport, preferring instead to draw a line under the ordeal rather than initiate another lengthy probe. Evidentiary hurdles and strategic threats Any new investigation faces significant logistical obstacles. The original charges relied heavily on a trove of leaked emails published by Der Spiegel in 2018. Rival clubs acknowledge that securing the same level of hard evidence for the post-2018 period remains highly unlikely. Despite this, the looming threat of a secondary probe is being viewed by some executives as a strategic bargaining chip. There is a belief that threatening further action could pressure City into accepting their impending punishment, preventing them from endlessly dragging out the current case with appeals. This proposed secondary scrutiny covers a highly successful era for the club. The eight-year period in question coincides with Pep Guardiola delivering six Premier League titles, raising the stakes significantly for the division. item.title: ‘A lot of lies’: Bruno Fernandes clarifies Carrick situation as Man United end winless run
item.description: ‘A lot of lies’: Bruno Fernandes clarifies Carrick situation as Man United end winless run Bruno Fernandes has hit out at media lies around what has been happening behind the scenes at Manchester United . Fernandes scored from the penalty spot as Manchester United recovered from two goals down to beat Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night, ending the club's nine-game winless run in all competitions. United's poor form has piled the pressure on Michael Carrick's position as manager, while Fernandes has been in the headlines for comments made about Carrick. The Portugal international criticised the club's tactics during a European defeat at Como last month, and was dropped to the bench for the following fixture against Bournemouth. Fernandes has dismissed reports that he and Carrick held clear-the-air talks in the aftermath, insisting his removal from the team was due to poor performances. The 32-year-old added that Manchester United have had to navigate a 'tough' period featuring 'a lot of lies' in the media, but said he retains belief in the manager and his teammates to turn things around. "We don’t need to save anyone’s job. The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It’s something we needed as a group of players, together with the staff," he said. "We’ve been working so hard to get out of this situation, all together. It’s been tough. There’s been a lot of speculation in the media, a lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club. "Between me and the manager, there were reports that we had cleared the air afterwards, when none of that happened. The manager made the decision to put me on the bench because I wasn’t performing that well. "Everyone felt that was a punishment for the words I’d said, and if it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions. I have to accept them and move forward with that. It doesn’t change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club, and it doesn’t change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me."

item.title: Kone aiming to recover in time for Sassuolo
item.description: Kone aiming to recover in time for Sassuolo Roma needs its big names. In the league, they’ve managed to do without them, winning and convincing even without some of their brightest stars. But the comeback by Manchester United revealed a problem: when the game gets tough and tense, the Giallorossi risk losing their bearings. This is primarily a mental, rather than physical, factor that Gasperini will need to work on. In the meantime, however, a helping hand could come from the infirmary. As Il Tempo reports, Koné is fast approaching his return for Saturday’s match against Sassuolo. Dybala is also hoping to be there: the Argentine has resumed training on the pitch and aims to be available again as soon as possible. Gasperini hopes to count on the two. Even if seeing them from the start seems pure utopia. But having them—even if only on the bench—makes all the difference in the world. And Gasperini knows it.

item.title: Is Serie A Europe's most exciting league?! Italian football might just be on the rise again after hitting rock bottom
item.description: Serie A GFX - GOAL The Italian top-flight has fallen a long way since its heyday in the 1990s, but there are signs that it's on the rise again Exactly three weeks ago, it felt as if Italian football had hit rock bottom. Just over six months after the national team had embarrassingly failed to qualify for a third consecutive World Cup, all four Serie A sides lost on the same Champions League matchday for the first time ever. There may have been some mitigating circumstances - Roma, for example, had been excellent for all but the final 10 minutes of their dramatic defeat by Real Madrid, while Como were playing just their second game in the competition - but the optics were undeniably awful for a country that hasn't had a European Cup winner for 16 years. Giovanni Malago nonetheless warned against making "blunt, sweeping states" regarding the state of Serie A , with the special administrator of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) arguing that "[These four defeats] do not represent a fair reflection of our football." And one could easily argue that he's already been proven correct. While Roma, Como, Inter and Napoli all winning their very next Champions League games the following week by no means signified that Italian football is actually in rude health, reports of its death were greatly exaggerated - and for three main reasons... 'Oldest stadiums in Europe' UEFA has threatened to strip Italy of the right to co-host Euro 2032 if its proposed venues are not up to scratch The principal problem with Italian football is that none of the game's major stakeholders are really ever willing to work together for the greater good. Almost everyone is motivated solely by self-interest, making progress impossible. As Alessandro Del Piero said during one of the many media-led inquests into Italy's latest World Cup qualification debacle, "Fundamentally, we think only about saving our own asses." However, there is one thing that everyone agrees on: the vast majority of Serie A stadiums are unworthy of elite-level sporting events. Napoli, for example, have won two titles in the past three years and yet club president Aureli De Laurentiis has repeatedly referred to their home ground as "a toilet". Why? Because the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, like so many other arenas, hasn't been significantly upgraded or redeveloped since Italy last hosted the World Cup - in 1990. That's about to change, though... at least in theory. When the FIGC confirmed its possible venues for Euro 2032 just last month, it was immediately noted that of the 14 contenders listed , only one (Juventus' Allianz Stadium) was actually ready to host games in its current guise. The other 13 had yet to be fully redeveloped - or even built - which obviously raised an awful lot of eyebrows. item.title: “STAY AWAY”, “We Not Interested”: Fans Vehemently Reject Brian Kelly as Former LSU Coach Admits He Wants FSU Job
item.description: Brian Kelly © IMAGN The Florida State Seminoles are searching for a new head coach after firing Mike Norvell following a 3-5 start to the season. Former LSU Tigers head coach Brian Kelly has entered the conversation while discussing the vacant position on SiriusXM’s College Sports Radio. Kelly, who called himself “unemployed” after LSU fired him midway through the 2025 season, said it would be an honor to take the job at Florida State, citing the Seminoles’ tradition, history, and fanbase. “Yeah, I mean, look, when you’re talking to an unemployed football coach, every job’s a great job, you know? But Florida State, look, I’ve got a great history with Florida State, great games,” Kelly said Monday. “I know what that’s like: the history and tradition of Florida State, playing in that state, and the fan base. So anytime you have an incredibly brand-driven, great tradition and history, there’s a want and desire to be part of somebody that has had that success and, certainly, leading that program, from anyone’s perspective, would be an honor and privilege.” However, fans aren’t happy with the prospect of Kelly becoming the new head coach of Florida State. “STAY AWAY FROM BRIAN KELLY!!!!!!!!! WE DON’T WANT BRIAN KELLY!!!!!” one fan wrote. “We’re not interested in him,” one fan commented. “Can’t believe this isn’t @No3sports. No way the bk killer thinks he actually has a chance,” one fan reacted. “How to end up in even more debt. Hire Brian Kelly,” one fan joked. “Yes! Please hire Brian Kelly so you can be disappointed for the next 4 years and fire him next!” one fan wrote. “I’d rather have Willie Taggart,” one fan added. “Going from Norvell to Brian Kelly would be something 😂” one fan noted. For now, FSU has appointed Rick Stockstill as the interim head coach. Kelly’s overall head-coaching record is 297-109-2 across stints with Grand Valley State, Central Michigan, Cincinnati, Notre Dame and LSU. Two Head Coaches Deny Florida State Job Rumors Brian Kelly Links Himself Even as Brian Kelly expressed his interest in becoming the next Florida State head coach, two head coaches have distanced themselves from the rumor. The two coaches are Missouri’s Eli Drinkwitz and Duke’s Manny Diaz. During his press conference ahead of Missouri’s game against Texas, Drinkwitz ruled himself out of the candidacy for the Seminoles’ job. “I’m not a candidate at Florida State,” Drinkwitz said . “I want to clear that up. item.title: Michael Carrick hails Old Trafford’s “magic” as Manchester United roar back to beat Roma
item.description: Michael Carrick hails Old Trafford’s “magic” as Manchester United roar back to beat Roma Michael Carrick has said the magic of Old Trafford helped Manchester United produce a stunning comeback to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League. Manchester United ended their winless run in dramatic fashion on Tuesday night, as Carrick's side recovered from two goals down to beat the Serie A side. Bruno Fernandes scored from the penalty spot to kickstart the comeback, before a late double from Matheus Cunha , who was later sent off, snapped the club's winless run. Reflecting at full-time, Carrick said his squad spoke about the 'magic' that Old Trafford can produce on big European nights. “It was a good night. A lot of credit to the players, for starters, showing that character and that quality when we needed it, and the supporters. “This place does incredible things. There’s magic here and we spoke about it at half-time," he said. “I thought we grew into it in the first half, actually, after giving the goals away too easily. We spoke at half-time about how this place can change, and it only takes one moment. The boys made the most of every little opportunity, really, and were fantastic in the end.” The win eases some of the mounting pressure on Carrick, who was asked whether the result can be a turning point in the club's season - and his future. The 45-year-old was keen to stress that Manchester United must build on what was a positive night. “It’s one game, so it depends on what happens next. We’ve got to capitalise on that. “But tonight, the boys showed an awful lot. I thought we came out in the second half and, unfortunately, with Carlos [Baleba] having to go off, Youri [Tielemans] came on the pitch and I thought he was fantastic. He showed everything that he is as a personality and as a character. He’s experienced, to step into a game like that. “The boys just went with the flow, and you could feel how positive it was. It was nice to see this place like that again.”

item.title: Tributes pour in for Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel as Raphinha sends 'message of strength' to family
item.description: Tributes have flooded in for Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died on Tuesday from injuries sustained in an on-field collision. The 30-year-old suffered a cardiac arrest in a clash with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono in a Spanish second-tier match on Monday and was rushed to hospital, with the match subsequently abandoned. Although Tenerife later released a statement saying he was stable, his condition worsened in the early hours of Tuesday and he died at 8am. Fans have congregated outside Tenerife’s home stadium, the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez, to lay flowers and light candles below a picture of the late player, and a farewell service will be held on Saturday at the ground which will be open to supporters. The club announced six days of official mourning during which all club activities are suspended, while players, staff and officials will attend his funeral. A minute’s silence was held before each of Tuesday night’s Champions League fixtures and will take place before all other Uefa fixtures this week. Barcelona ’s Raphinha , who scored twice during their Champions League win over Aston Villa, said afterwards: “Today I don't want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus - may he rest in peace. “From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family.” Fellow Spaniard Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta addressed the “heartbreaking” death in a press conference on Tuesday, saying: “To see a colleague lose his life in such a manner, it's beyond any words that I can put today”. Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho said: “I think it's something very shocking for the world in general, so imagine for the world of football, for people like us who are on the pitch competing every day.” He also expressed his concern for Owono, who was given a straight red card after the collision and who has since deactivated his Instagram account. Mourinho said it was a “very, very, very difficult moment” for the Andorra keeper. Spanish police have opened a “routine” investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter ; under national law any death which is deemed non-natural automatically triggers an investigation. The Spanish Football Federation announced the postponement of Tuesday’s Copa del Rey and Copa del Reina matches in honour of De Miguel. “We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends and loved ones, as well as to Club Deportivo Tenerife and all its fans, whom we accompany in these moments of great sorrow,” it said. De Miguel made his professional debut in 2015 for Leganes B and played for several Spanish clubs before joining Tenerife from Castellon in 2025. He signed a three-year contract with Tenerife last summer and helped the club earn promotion back to the Segunda Division, scoring 11 goals in 29 games.

item.title: “Was amazing”: Wayne Rooney lauds Man United comeback after “terrible” first half
item.description: “Was amazing”: Wayne Rooney lauds Man United comeback after “terrible” first half Manchester United came out on top 3-2 against AS Roma in the Champions League on a rollercoaster night at Old Trafford. The match The first half was United at their worst, and unfortunately, this has been a regular sight this season. They were chaotic and lifeless as the Italian visitors roared into a 2-0 lead inside the first 17 minutes. The home side could hardly muster much of a response in the first 45 minutes and were deservedly behind. Nonetheless, Michael Carrick’s side roared back into life in the second half, creating numerous chances before finally completing the comeback 3-2 for a much-needed victory, not just in the Champions League but also for the team’s season. Wayne Rooney’s thoughts Speaking to Amazon Prime (via football365.com ) at half-time, Rooney tore into Bruno Fernandes. When referencing the Romans’ first goal he said, “you’re in the Champions League and with all the talk and criticism the team have got, you were expecting some sort of reaction. There was nothing, absolutely nothing.” He continued, “Roma took the ball and were more aggressive, no one on the United team put a tackle in. They were really struggling down the left-hand side.” Continuing his dissection of the goal he explained, “you just want to see something, some sort of fight and passion and desire to win the football game but there was nothing. For the first goal, if you’re playing in a system, when Dalot goes higher, Bruno should go into that position. He has to run back, you’re the captain of the football club, run back and take responsibility.” He implored the side to play as a team and cover a teammate if they find themselves out of position. Rooney added, “I feel so sorry for the fans because they don’t know what to do. They’ve not been in this position for years, they don’t know whether to get behind the team or to get on their backs. I feel so sorry for them.” Nonetheless, the second half was much more of what every United fan wants to see, and Rooney was also more positive after the match. He explained, “the second-half was amazing, they were front-footed and they deserved to win the game in the end. The first half was terrible but we saw the passion and fight we wanted in the second half. The crowd got right behind the team and you felt like they could go on to win the game.” Speaking specifically on the captain, Rooney stated, “Bruno Fernandes has shown a bit of passion in defending himself on what he thought was right, but more importantly we have seen that passion and fight on the pitch because the first half was terrible. item.title: “I’m not Mo Salah” – Bradley Barcola speaks defiantly about his big-money Liverpool transfer
item.description: “I’m not Mo Salah” – Bradley Barcola speaks defiantly about his big-money Liverpool transfer Bradley Barcola has said that he doesn’t feel any pressure to try and emulate Mo Salah at Liverpool and is instead focusing on creating his own legacy at Anfield. At the end of the summer, the Reds spent an initial £106m (potentially rising to £123m, via The Athletic ) to sign the French winger from Paris Saint-Germain, with the 24-year-old effectively brought in as the right-sided replacement for the Egyptian King. It took the new signing seven matches to get off the mark for LFC, with that famine turning to feast in the form of a hat-trick against LASK in mid-October, and he’s followed that up with assists in the wins over Brentford and Brighton ( Transfermarkt ). Barcola not feeling pressure to emulate Salah In an interview with Sky Sports , Barcola defiantly insisted that he doesn’t feel a burden to emulate Salah or repay the substantial transfer fee paid for him, with his sole focus being to make his ‘own mark’ and let his performances do the talking. The France winger said: “First of all, I wasn’t the one who decided the transfer fee, so that’s not been my problem. “Regarding Mo Salah, he’s a legend here, a huge one. He’s done big things here and, for that, I have an enormous respect for him, but it’s not pressure for me at all. “I’m not Mo Salah, so I’m going to try to contribute whatever I can to the club and make my own mark on its history. I don’t feel any pressure about that.” (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Barcola has shown promising signs so far at Liverpool Whoever was signed as the effective replacement for the legendary Egyptian was always going to face inevitable comparisons with our former no.11, but such were the standards set by Salah that striving to emulate him would be near-impossible. Nobody is expecting Barcola to match the Trabzonspor man’s 257-goal tally for Liverpool over a nine-year period. As the Frenchman acknowledged, his job is simply to deliver the best that he can for the Reds. There have been some moments to forget in his first few weeks on Merseyside, such as the missed sitter against Brentford last month, but he also conjured up a tremendous assist for Alexander Isak’s winning goal in the same match. The 24-year-old might’ve drawn a blank against Arsenal on Sunday, but his direct running along the left flank was difficult for the Gunners to contain during the first half in particular, offering the kind of proactive threat that we love to see from wingers playing for LFC. Salah was a unique figure at Liverpool, and Barcola doesn’t strictly have to emulate what the Egyptian has done in order to be regarded as a success at Anfield in time to come. We’ve seen glimpses of what he can offer to the Reds, and time is very much on his side to build upon that promising start.

item.title: Jets Make NHL History With Stunning Comeback Win Against Habs
item.description: Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images Getty Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images Getty The Winnipeg Jets appeared destined for what would have been a 10th straight loss, finding themselves trailing by a 4-0 score against the Montreal Canadiens at Bell Centre on Tuesday night. But then, suddenly, everything clicked and resulted in a stunning and historic turnaround, not only ending their miserable losing skid but also setting a new NHL record. The Jets scored five unanswered goals to complete a 5-4 comeback win despite trailing 4-0 with 2:39 left in the third period. And in doing so, they officially set the mark for the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history. The Winnipeg Jets Set NHL History After Stunning Comeback Victory Over Montreal Getty Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images The Jets trailed 4-0 against the Canadiens on Tuesday night thanks to goals from Owen Beck, Josh Anderson, and a pair from Cole Caufield. However, the Jets got the comeback started thanks to the first NHL goal from Tyrel Bauer at 17:21 of the third period, followed by a goal from Morgan Barron at 18:03 to make Montreal nervous. Kyle Connor then scored twice in a matter of 27 seconds, shocking the sellout crowd at Bell Centre that thought their Canadiens had two points in the bag. Shortly into overtime, it was Dylan Samberg ripping a shot past goaltender Jacob Fowler, completing the historic comeback and silencing Canadiens fans everywhere. Before Tuesday night, the Canadiens had won 448 of the last 449 times that they led by at least four goals entering the third period; their only unsuccessful attempt came in the form of an overtime loss against the Minnesota North Stars in 1984. Additionally, the most recent four-goal comeback this late in the third period took place in 2007 by the Los Angeles Kings , who trailed 4-0 at the 52:46 mark of the third period against the Dallas Stars. What’s more, it’s also the fastest four goals that the Jets have scored in club history. Could This Win Save Head Coach Scott Arniel’s Job? With the win, the Jets improved their record to 5-8-3 – and more importantly, halted a nine-game losing skid. During their losing streak, whispers have grown louder concerning the job security of head coach Scott Arniel, who made it clear that he’s not thinking about that and still considers the Jets “in the hunt”. “I really don’t care about that. I really don’t. I’m so happy that we won tonight. We got that win,” Arniel said. “To me, we’re still in the hunt.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Jets Make NHL History With Stunning Comeback Win Against Habs appeared first on HEAVY .

item.description: Fabián Ruiz scores twice as PSG hit Villarreal for six in record-quick start Paris Saint-Germain scored four goals faster than any side in Champions League history on their way to a 6-0 win at La Cerámica. The defeat leaves Iñigo Pérez taking the blame and Villarreal with one win from four league-phase games. Fabián Ruiz scored twice as Paris Saint-Germain beat Villarreal 6-0 at the Estadio de la Cerámica on Tuesday 3 November 2026. The visitors led 4-0 at the break in round four of the Champions League league stage. João Neves opened the scoring in the ninth minute. Désiré Doué added a second three minutes later from a Maghnes Akliouche pass. Senny Mayulu struck in the 13th minute. Ruiz then converted another Akliouche assist. Four goals in 16 minutes set a Champions League mark That fourth goal arrived after 16 minutes and two seconds, beIN SPORTS reported. No team had ever scored four times faster in the competition. By half-time PSG had eight shots on target to Villarreal’s one. Ruiz added his second in the 50th minute, set up by Vitinha. Flashscore described it as only the second time he had scored twice in a game for PSG. He finished with a rating of 9.81. David Boly completed the rout in the 78th minute, with Neves providing the assist. The 17-year-old was making his Champions League debut. He scored four minutes after coming off the bench. The numbers matched the scoreline. PSG completed 677 accurate passes to Villarreal’s 237. Their expected goals reached 2.75 against 0.74. Péter Gulácsi made six saves to keep the margin at six. Luis Enrique managed this without four regulars. Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé, Nuno Mendes and Marquinhos all missed the trip through injury. The win was PSG’s 10th in a row. It also took them to 14 European Cup matches unbeaten, equalling the longest such run by a French club. After four matchdays, they were the only club in the league phase on 12 points. Pérez takes the blame as La Cerámica empties Iñigo Pérez left Alberto Moleiro and Georges Mikautadze on the bench. He chose a less attacking line-up than usual. By the sixth goal the stadium was half empty. The fans who stayed whistled the home side again. Pérez blamed himself for the biggest mistakes. He said his side had got their idea of how to play PSG wrong. He added that they had the wrong mindset after conceding. He also defended Carlos Macià, who had only just turned 18 and faced Vitinha. Pérez put the youngster’s struggles down to his own tactical plan. At his press conference he would not discuss his own future. He said the squad was devastated and needed to focus on finding solutions. Villarreal’s European campaign has stalled. They lost 3-2 at Borussia Dortmund on 8 September. A 3-1 home win over Napoli followed on 13 October. They then lost 4-3 at Liverpool on 20 October. Domestically, their previous outing was a 1-0 defeat by Espanyol. item.description: Arsenal handed double injury boost before Slavia Prague trip Arsenal head to Slavia Prague with William Saliba back in contention and Max Dowman available again, giving Mikel Arteta more options for Wednesday night. Mikel Arteta confirmed the defender played 45 minutes in a behind-closed-doors game last week and is now ready to be considered, although whether he is used will depend on what Arsenal need. “Yes, he’s in a really good place,” Arteta said . “I think the process and the timings and in the manner that the injury has been dealt with, and especially the feelings that Willy has been having along the way, they’ve been very, very positive. “So, his evolution has been as expected, which is not always the case.
